claims.statement: Polish and EU procurement rules permit groups of economic operators to bid jointly without adopting a special legal form merely to submit the bid, while allowing a representative or lead member and proportionate group-specific performance conditions.

Under Polish procurement law, licenses, experience, and professional capabilities pooled by a joint bid must be connected to the member that will perform the work requiring them, and reliance on third-party resources must show real tender-specific access.

Joint bidders in Poland are jointly and severally liable for contract performance and performance security; above-threshold bid security can be up to 3% of contract value and performance security is generally up to 5% of the offered price or maximum nominal obligation.

European Commission competition guidance treats a bidding consortium as generally non-restrictive when it enables a project the parties could not undertake individually, but requires case-specific assessment when members could bid independently and limits shared information to what is necessary.

Poland's official e-Zamówienia platform already provides free BZP/TED search, offer submission, and notice subscriptions, and the state procurement-policy portal includes a consortium module for partner-finding.
Nationwide turnkey photovoltaic general contractors already market end-to-end design, construction, and service to Polish business buyers, creating an incumbent response to a new installer network.

contrary_evidence: Joint bidding does not make a thin coordinator qualified: licenses and experience must be tied to the member actually performing the relevant work, and actual resource access must be documented.
Members face joint and several performance liability and material bid and performance-security exposure, so a low-capital coordinator cannot assume member failure is ring-fenced.
Exclusive mandates among firms capable of independent bids can raise Article 101 concerns; the safest wedge is scopes no member can undertake alone and minimum-necessary information sharing.
Official Polish platforms already provide free tender feeds, subscriptions, offer workflows, and consortium partner-finding.
Established nationwide EPC contractors already sell turnkey business projects and have stronger references and balance sheets.

economics.acquisition_route: Free official BZP/TED feeds identify opportunities; family-installer proof, wholesalers, trade referrals, and the government consortium module can recruit member supply
economics.capital_required_pln: Unvalidated. The v1 95,000 PLN placeholder cannot be treated as sufficient for a medium framework: Polish law allows bid security up to 3% for above-threshold procedures and performance security generally up to 5%, although non-cash guarantees may be available subject to underwriting.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis only. The v1 30 million PLN managed-volume path lacks evidence for win rate, take rate, contribution margin, guarantee capacity, repeat awards, or valuation.
economics.founder_time: A single narrow pilot may fit part-time; concurrent bids and live multi-region delivery require delegated legal, bid, finance, and field-QA roles rather than 15-25 founder hours as a stable operating assumption
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unknown. The v1 estimate of 35-55% of retained revenue is unsupported and must include losing-bid cost, procurement counsel, insurance, guarantee fees, field QA, disputes, defect reserves, and unrecovered member failure.
economics.payback: Unknown. A win does not establish payback until security, mobilization, milestone timing, payment delays, defects, and member payouts are modeled from an actual specification and contract
economics.pricing: Unvalidated. No authoritative source supports retaining 10-18% of contract value; price a contract-specific bid-management and QA fee or prime margin only after member quotations, warranty allocation, guarantee cost, buyer payment schedule, and competitive bid analysis.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Frameworks and repeat members may recur after strong delivery, but references attach to actual performers and buyer re-award is not assured

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Verified regional capacity, tender-specific resource commitments, member qualification files, accepted completion evidence, and delivery references can reduce bid assembly time and increase credibility
fingerprint.customer: Public and private multi-site buyers whose geography or service levels exceed one small installer's capacity, and qualified regional installers seeking access to those scopes
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Use free BZP/TED search and subscription data for opportunity detection, while the family installer, trade referrals, wholesalers, and delivery references recruit and qualify members
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Tender qualification, documented capacity commitments, bid preparation, lead representation, work allocation to qualified members, common QA and evidence, invoicing administration, and SLA management
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The buyer pays the awarded contractor group or prime; a disclosed, contract-specific coordination and QA fee or margin is paid under the members' agreement as milestones are accepted
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A tender or multi-site request requires combined geography, references, licenses, staffing, guarantees, evidence, or service levels that no recruited member can provide alone

founder_fit: The parents' installer supplies a bounded operating reference and domain knowledge
Tender detection, document normalization, and capacity matching fit automation and data skills
It remains part-time only if procurement-law review, bid administration, financial control, and field QA are delegated before multiple live bids
risks: Joint and several liability could expose solvent members or the lead to another member's failure.
Bid and performance security or working capital can exceed available founder funds.
Overbroad exclusivity or information sharing among potential independent bidders can create competition-law risk.
A member's missing license, reference, capacity, safety performance, or documentation can invalidate the bid or damage delivery.
Incumbent EPCs can bid directly with stronger balance sheets, references, and buyer trust.

structure.commercial_archetype: Managed joint contractor and tender consortium
structure.control_point: Tender-specific, legally reviewed member commitments that prove actual access to qualified regional capacity and bind role, price, QA, and delivery responsibility
structure.critical_dependency: The team must lawfully combine qualifications and resources, finance bid and performance security, price joint liability, and deliver consistently across all members

thesis: Form tender-specific teams of vetted regional renewable and electrical installers only where no member can credibly deliver the whole scope alone. Secure documented capacity commitments, allocate licensed work to the member whose qualifications support it, appoint a lead representative, standardize evidence and QA, and price coordination into the joint offer. The defensible asset would be verified deployable capacity and delivery history, not tender alerts or a generic partner directory.
title: Installer Joint-Tender Authority Network
uncertainties: No installer has signed a tender-specific capacity, pricing, exclusivity, QA, or joint-liability commitment.
No buyer has accepted a newly formed coordinator or member network as prime or lead.
The 10-18% take rate and 35-55% retained-revenue margin have no evidence.
Tender-by-tender turnover, reference, license, insurance, bond, warranty, and payment requirements are unknown.
No bank or insurer has quoted bid or performance guarantees for the proposed entity and members.
No actual bid establishes win probability, coordination hours, member pricing discipline, or defect reserve.
